_note: Sample activity from sxp_activity_criteria (Databricks, production.supply_analytics). Scalar fields are verbatim. The source file's 94-row `defect_records` array is not reproduced per-booking — the page has nowhere to show individual rows — but it is now summarised into details.quality-rate.disruptions below, the same treatment the nine real fixtures give their booking-level data. Full file: ~/Downloads/activity_21293_full.json
_note_next_award_date: NOT from the export — added to drive the status-banner copy, which names the date the badge would appear. The criteria deck lists award cadence as an open question, so this is a placeholder. Set to the end of the assessment period, on the assumption the badge is awarded when the period closes.
_note_window: window_start/window_end are the intended assessment period (Jul 1, 2026 – Jan 1, 2027), not the export's own window (2026-04-18 – 2026-10-14). The metrics below were measured over the export's window, so the period label and the numbers come from different ranges in this fixture.
_note_details: NOT from the export, and INVENTED. sxp_activity_criteria holds one rating for the whole window, so there is no monthly series to read — same gap documented for every other fixture's `trend`. These six points are hand-written to show the chart in its passing state (757:29057): every month clears the 4.6 bar, so no month is shaded, and the mean is 4.6617 against the row's real rating_in_window of 4.6599. Treat the shape as illustrative; only the average is anchored to anything real.

defects.name: Activity Not As Advertised
defects.description: The activity delivered did not match the description.
recommendations: Review the description of your activity so travelers know what to expect
Ensure your photos accurately reflect the experience

defects.name: Supplier Not Responsive
defects.description: The traveler contacted you and did not get a reply in time.
recommendations: Check your inbox daily, including the day before travel
Keep the phone number on your listing one a traveler can actually reach

defects.name: Activity Oversubscribed
defects.description: More travelers were booked than the activity could take.
recommendations: Set group-size caps that match what you can actually staff
Keep capacity in sync when you sell the same slot on other channels

defects.name: Supplier Cancellation (non-FM)
defects.description: You cancelled the booking for a reason within your control.
recommendations: Close availability you cannot staff rather than cancelling after travelers book
Keep availability in sync when you sell the same slot on other channels

defects.name: Extra Charge
defects.description: The traveler was asked to pay more than the booked price.
recommendations: Include every mandatory fee in the price shown on GetYourGuide
List genuinely optional extras in the Important Information section

defects.name: Unclear Meeting Point Location
defects.description: The meeting point description was unclear, or wrong.
recommendations: Verify the address is findable in a map app and add a meeting point photo
Include landmarks or directions from the nearest transport stop

defects.name: Guide Language Wrong or Low Proficiency
defects.description: The guide did not speak the language originally booked for.
recommendations: Confirm which languages each guide can deliver and keep the option list in sync
Remove languages you cannot staff reliably rather than risk a mismatch

defects.name: Unsuitable For Disabled Customers
defects.description: The activity could not accommodate a traveler's accessibility needs.
recommendations: State accessibility limitations plainly in the Important Information section
Describe terrain, steps and transport so travelers can judge suitability

activity_title: Murano & Burano Guided Tour by Private Boat with Glassmaking
_note_supplier_name: NOT from the export — sxp_activity_criteria carries supplier_id only. Looked up from dwh.dim_supplier.company_name on user_id = 363.
_note_details_rating: INVENTED, not from the export. sxp_activity_criteria holds one rating for the whole window — there is no monthly series anywhere — so these six points are generated around the row's real rating_in_window (4.6599) with a fixed zero-sum shape, scaled so the series stays under 5.0 and clears the 4.60 bar, matching crit_rating. Only the mean is anchored to anything real; the month-to-month shape is illustrative.
_note_details_quality_rate: INVENTED, not from the export. sxp_activity_criteria holds one quality defect rate for the whole window, so these six points are generated around the row's real value (1.2142%) with a fixed zero-sum shape, scaled to stay at or above zero and stays under the 1.50% bar, matching crit_defect_rate. Only the mean is anchored to anything real.
_note_details_quality_disruptions: REAL, unlike the trend above it. Built from this activity's own rows in production.supply_analytics.sxp_booking_defect, counting DISTINCT booking_id per tag and filtered to the tag set the criteria deck defines for this metric: the 9 quality tags + Supplier Cancellation (non-FM). The tour's rows carry 21 distinct tags in all; the 13 outside that set (Too Crowded, Duration Not As Advertised, Transport Low Quality, Audio Guide Broken, Confirmation Not Received and so on) are excluded, exactly as the nine real fixtures do. Tags are ordered by count descending, which is the only thing the order conveys — see _caveat_counts_not_shown. Copy for all tags but one is reused verbatim from the existing fixtures, which took it from the design; `Supplier Cancellation (non-FM)` had no copy anywhere in the repo, so its description and recommendations are written here in the same voice and are NOT from the design.
_caveat_counts_not_shown: The `count` on each defect is provenance, not display data. criteria-render.js strips counts before handing the list to the shared defect-cards module, so no number reaches the supplier — the shared module reads `count` only to fill '{count}' in a recommended-action title, and falls back to 'recent' when it is absent. Counts are kept in this file because they determine the display order and record what the query returned.
_caveat_counts_do_not_reconcile: These tags cover 27 distinct bookings against a quality_defect_bookings of 61 — they explain under half the rate shown above them. This is the sxp_booking_defect gap documented in CLAUDE.md, not a filtering mistake here: the table's latest travel_date is 2026-09-14 while the criteria window runs to 2026-10-14, and even inside the covered range its distinct-booking counts fall short of the aggregates. The shortfall is wider here than in the other real fixtures (italy-defect is 8 against 9), which is the main argument for never printing the counts.
